items.excerpt: Two dueling surveys on AI audiobook narration: a Spoken-commissioned study found 61% of listeners mistook AI voices for human and preferred them in multi-character scenes, while an Audio Publishers Association study shows willingness to try AI narration fell from 70% (2025) to 61% (2026), with human narration still preferred overall.

items.excerpt: At the 35th IPA Congress in Kuala Lumpur, three sessions on children's publishing argued that the format and quality of content — not AI itself — shape how digital-native kids read, and pressed publishers on closing a widening global literacy gap.

items.excerpt: Publishers including Cengage, Elsevier and Hachette have filed a class-action suit against Google, accusing it of illegally copying millions of books to train its Gemini AI service — the latest front in the fight over whether published books can be used as AI training data.

items.excerpt: Amazon expanded Kindle Translate, its free AI-powered translation service for KDP indie authors, from two language pairs to six languages (English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese). Authors can create, price and publish fully formatted machine-translated editions in a few clicks, with automatic accuracy checks before publication.
